summary: Security-critical paths: (1) stdin JSON parser — 256 KiB cap enforced BEFORE json.loads; depth cap 3, per-string cap 10 KiB, strict key allowlist. (2) preview path handling — CACHE_DIR resolved once, mkdir+chmod 0o700, NamedTemporaryFile inside, post-write Path.resolve() and parent-equality guard before any webbrowser.open. (3) webbrowser invocation — file:// URI with a path that has just passed the guard. No shell, no eval, no subprocess.

findings.finding: sys.stdin.buffer.read(_STDIN_READ_LIMIT) reads up to 256 KiB + 1 bytes. If the reader returns exactly that many, we refuse without parsing. This is correct BEFORE-parse gating.

Validator explicitly rejects unknown top-level keys and unknown block keys, preventing prototype-pollution-style payloads. Heading.level pinned to {3,4}; image/video URLs are treated as strings here (renderer is the one that enforces the https:// scheme allowlist).
CACHE_DIR is created with mode=0o700 and then explicitly chmod'd to 0o700 (Python's mkdir mode is ignored on existing dirs). A belt-and-suspenders call. Smoke-verified: drwx------.

webbrowser.open(f'file://{path}') — path has just been validated against CACHE_DIR. path comes from tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(prefix='hw-', suffix='.html') and has been through Path.resolve(). No symbolic-link, no `..`, no shell interpolation. Acceptable.

cmd_stage writes 'invalid JSON: {err}' to stderr; json.JSONDecodeError's repr can contain a short snippet of the bad payload. If an operator pipes a secret into stdin by mistake, a fragment could surface. Risk is low (operator-only tool, local stdin). No action.
Path-guard uses Path equality (path.parent != CACHE_DIR). Both sides are resolved Path objects — `/x/` vs `/x` style string divergence is handled. Tested with test_preview_path_guard_escape_aborts.
